objective: TIME-POLISH PPO on Jungle1: start from a BC champion that already wins 98.56% of episodes (9856/10000, fastest win 891 ticks, median win 3833 ticks at training hold; lineage.bc_champion_eval_10k_tail) and optimize EXPECTED COMPLETION TIME. Why this is a different problem from the five failed exploration-era PPO runs (all lineage-linked below): those runs initialized from policies that essentially never won (0-17 training wins over thousands of episodes), so the +10 win bonus was invisible to the gradient, score shaping hijacked the return, and every run ended FAIL or was stopped. Here the win bonus appears in ~99% of episodes, so the return's residual variance is dominated by the TIME term and the time gradient is well-posed: PPO is polishing a working policy's speed, not searching for wins. The time signal is strengthened 5x (time_penalty_per_native_tick -0.0005): a median win now costs ~-1.9 in time against +10 win, so a 500-tick speedup is worth +0.25 per episode (~2.6% of episode return, versus ~0.5% under the old -0.0001) while winning still strictly dominates everything (see trainer_v2.reward_alignment). Success is measured in median winning ticks at a win-rate floor; SCORE IS NOT A SUCCESS METRIC. The win-rate floor is guarded by early_stop_rules clause (a).

reward_resolution.how_the_validator_resolves_it: v2._configs_v2 hands environment.reward_profile to v2._reward_config_v2 (tools/train_overnight_multilevel_v2.py lines 320-356): each of profile_id, win_reward, failure_reward, time_penalty_per_native_tick present in the mapping OVERRIDES the v2 defaults (win-time-score-truncation-neutral-v2, +10/-10/-0.0001); score_progress_reward_cap is NOT read from the reward_profile - it is owned by TrainerV2Config (trainer_v2.score_progress_reward_cap, here 1.0), so one receipt governs it. profile_id is a label: WinFirstRewardConfig.__post_init__ (src/zuma_rl/human_speedrun.py lines 71-89) checks only that it is non-empty; there is no registry check anywhere in the v2/v2b path, so this document assigns a NEW id that truthfully describes the changed profile instead of re-using the v2 id whose name would now lie about the time term.
reward_resolution.ordering_guarantees: the composed training wrapper is DenseShapingObservableHumanSpeedrunWrapper; its _validate_reward_ordering (v2 lines 237-266) enforces minimum win return > maximum terminated-failure return: (10 + (-0.0005 x 12000)) = +4.0 > (-10 + 1.0) = -9.0, satisfied with margin 13.0. NOTE: the base HumanSpeedrunWrapper one-second dominance rule (human_speedrun.py lines 187-194) would REJECT cap 1.0 against -0.0005 (one second of time = 0.05 < 1.0); the v2 dense-shaping mixin deliberately drops exactly that rule, which is what makes this profile constructible without touching any frozen file.
reward_resolution.magnitude_rationale: 5x stronger clock signal. Median win (~3833 ticks at training hold, p50 of the 10k tail) costs ~-1.9 against +10 win, so time is ~19% of a median winning return instead of ~3.8% under -0.0001; a 500-tick improvement moves the return by +0.25 (~2.6%), comfortably above PPO advantage noise at batch 1024. Worst-case time-limit truncation (12000 ticks, truncation-neutral so NO -10 terminal) returns >= -6.0 + at most +1.0 shaping = about -5.0, still strictly below the WORST possible win (+10 - 6.0 = +4.0): finishing dominates farming and stalling everywhere in return space. A terminated loss pays -10 minus time, so dying fast is never rewarded either.

hold_ticks_decision.training_source: ParkSettleActionConfig.hold_ticks default (src/zuma_rl/park_settle_action_wrapper.py line 89). NO existing configuration path can set it for training: v2b's StackedMultiLevelSpeedrunEnvV2._make_env (tools/train_overnight_multilevel_v2b.py lines 151-160) calls make_stacked_macro_env without a park_settle_config, so make_stacked_macro_env (lines 108-140) constructs ParkSettleActionWrapper(env, config=None) and the dataclass default applies; on the v2 side neither TrainerV2Config (_CONFIG_FIELDS, v2 lines 179-189) nor the CLI (v2 build_parser / _cli_trainer_overrides lines 1278-1351) exposes any hold_ticks knob, and MultiLevelSpeedrunEnvV2._make_env (v2 lines 531-539) likewise never passes park_settle_config. Configuring hold 4 for training would therefore require editing frozen tools, which this campaign forbids - so TRAINING RUNS AT hold_ticks 8 and this asymmetry is preregistered rather than papered over.
hold_ticks_decision.evaluation_source: the paired 2k-seed A/B (lineage.hold_ab_receipts): hold 4 is ~90 ticks faster at the median (3720 vs 3810) with win rate within noise (0.9850 vs 0.9885) on identical seeds, and the search tool exposes hold_ticks per run (both A/B configs and both RUNNING lanes already use it). All per-checkpoint and final evals under this document run at hold_ticks 4.
hold_ticks_decision.asymmetry_note: train at 8, evaluate at 4. The A/B is direct evidence the policy transfers across hold settings without retraining (both arms >98% win); the wait-macro is a parked no-op whose length changes pacing, not aiming. If the trained policy's hold-4 eval win rate collapses while training telemetry stays healthy, that is a transfer failure and early_stop_rules clause (a) catches it.

early_stop_rules.checkpoint_grid_note: checkpoint_every 262144 with 40 envs -> SB3 CheckpointCallback save_freq = 262144 // 40 = 6553 vec-steps, i.e. checkpoints on a 262,120-macro-step grid (~11 checkpoints inside the 3M budget); each checkpoint gets the 16-seed eval below before the next checkpoint lands
early_stop_rules.checkpoint_eval_protocol: 16-seed held-out panel, seeds 1494001000..1494001015 (contiguous --seed-start 1494001000 --seed-count 16), hold_ticks 4, stack lags 0,4,8, deterministic masked predict, via tools/search_alphazuma_55_macro_speedrun_seeds_v1.py (sha256:64119b8de747405ed7b067240f2a8ec130df8b66ff9a295fd4e44ae02438e3dc) against the checkpoint zip; eval device chosen at eval time so as not to preempt the training on cuda:0; metrics recorded: wins/16, median winning ticks over the wins, shots_on_target_rate

clause_a_win_rate_floor.clause: if the 16-seed eval win rate is below 0.90 (i.e. 14/16 or fewer wins) at TWO CONSECUTIVE checkpoints, STOP the run and keep the best earlier checkpoint
clause_a_win_rate_floor.best_checkpoint_rule: best = highest 16-seed win rate; ties broken by lower median winning ticks; the BC init itself (8/8 on the first half of this panel, lineage.bc_champion_heldout_eval8) is the fallback if no checkpoint qualifies
clause_a_win_rate_floor.rationale: the premise of this run is a ~99%-win policy; if time pressure starts trading wins away faster than 0.90 on the held-out panel, the time gradient is eating the objective and continuing would repeat the exploration-era reward-hijack failure in mirror image

clause_b_stagnation_success.clause: if the median winning ticks of the 16-seed eval fails to improve on the best median observed so far at THREE CONSECUTIVE checkpoint evals, CONCLUDE THE RUN SUCCESSFULLY with the best checkpoint
clause_b_stagnation_success.best_checkpoint_rule: best = lowest median winning ticks among checkpoints whose 16-seed win rate is >= 0.90
clause_b_stagnation_success.rationale: time-polish saturates; three flat checkpoints (~786k steps) is the preregistered definition of converged, and stopping there banks the speed gain instead of grinding the win rate

trainer_v2.reward_alignment: cap 1.0 carried from the r3/r3b lineage (score shaping stays a discovery aid, never a rival to the +10 win bonus). TIME-POLISH delta: time_penalty_per_native_tick is -0.0005 (5x the v2 default), set via environment.reward_profile per reward_resolution. Arithmetic at Jungle1's max_ticks 12000: worst win = 10 - 6.0 = +4.0; best truncation (truncation-neutral) = about -6.0 + 1.0 = -5.0; best terminated failure = -10 + 1.0 - time < -9.0. Ordering: every win > every truncation > every terminated failure; median win (~3833 ticks) nets ~ +8.1 - 1.9 time makes speed the dominant residual signal on winning episodes, which is the entire point of this run.
trainer_v2.discounting_note: gamma applies PER MACRO STEP; the macro reward is the undiscounted per-tick sum over the ticks the macro consumed, so 0.999 per macro is roughly 0.999^(1/40) per native tick; truncation is reward-neutral (v2 wrapper), so a timed-out episode bootstraps instead of paying -10

runs.description: TIME-POLISH single-level sprint: macro-interface PPO fine-tune of the 98.6%-win BC champion on Jungle1 only, on cuda:0 (occupied by the finishing rta-big search at freeze; the 20-min launch margin in the schedule covers the handover), 40 workers, 5x time penalty, entropy 0.005 (between the fresh 0.01 and warm-start 2e-3 defaults: enough jitter to find faster lines, not enough to unlearn winning - the win-rate floor in early_stop_rules guards the downside), lr 1e-5 as in the whole macro-PPO lineage
runs.checkpoint_note: one macro step is one policy timestep (~20-70 native ticks); with 40 envs the callback grid floors to 262,120 steps (~11 checkpoints in the 3M budget). At the r3-era observed ~341 steps/s (shared-CPU worst case) 3M steps take ~2.4 h; the 6-h backstop is generous and the v2 callback stops at schedule.training_stop_utc regardless.
runs.budget_note: total_steps 3M is deliberately SMALL: this is a polish sprint from an already-winning init, not an exploration campaign; early_stop_rules clause (b) is expected to conclude the run before the budget or the wall clock does

evaluation_cadence.telemetry: wins/16, median winning ticks over wins, per-win tick list, shots, shots_on_target_rate (wrapper fidelity, expect ~1.0); score is recorded only as a liveness diagnostic, never a success metric
